stories.headline: Anthropic's Project Deal Shows AI Agent Quality Creates Invisible Economic Inequality in Marketplaces

key_facts.fact: Anthropic ran a marketplace experiment with 69 employees where Claude agents bought, sold, and negotiated personal belongings; agents completed 186 deals worth over $4,000 total.
key_facts.excerpt: For one week, we created a classified marketplace for employees in our San Francisco office... our 69 agents struck 186 deals across over 500 listed items, for a total transaction value of just over $4,000.

key_facts.fact: In a secret parallel experiment, users with the frontier model Claude Opus 4.5 completed ~2 more deals on average than those with the smaller Claude Haiku 4.5.
key_facts.excerpt: users with Opus completed about two more deals than Haiku users, on average.

key_facts.fact: When the same item was sold by Opus instead of Haiku, it went for $3.64 more on average; Opus sellers extracted $2.68 more per item and Opus buyers paid $2.45 less.
key_facts.excerpt: When an item was sold by Opus instead of Haiku, it went for $3.64 more on average... Opus as a seller extracts $2.68 more on average for the same item, and as a buyer pays $2.45 less.

key_facts.fact: Users with worse-performing agents did not notice their disadvantage; perceived fairness scores were nearly identical (4.05 for Opus deals vs 4.06 for Haiku) on a 7-point scale.
key_facts.excerpt: perceived fairness was essentially identical for deals conducted by either model (4.05 for deals done by Opus agents and 4.06 for deals done by Haiku, on the same 1 to 7 scale).

key_facts.fact: Aggressive user instructions made no statistically significant difference on outcomes; what mattered was which model represented you, not how you told it to negotiate.
key_facts.excerpt: users who instructed their agents to act aggressively didn't have a better chance of selling items, didn't sell their items for more, and didn't pay less for what they bought.

key_facts.fact: 46% of participants said they would pay for a similar AI agent commerce service in the future.
key_facts.excerpt: when we asked them if they'd be willing to pay for an agent like this, 46% said yes.

sources.title: Project Deal: our Claude-run marketplace experiment

key_facts.fact: President Trump is sending envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner to Islamabad on Saturday for talks with Iran, with VP JD Vance on 'standby'
key_facts.excerpt: President Donald Trump to send envoys to Pakistan, with JD Vance, who led talks with Iran in Islamabad nearly two weeks ago, on 'standby'

key_facts.fact: Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi landed in Islamabad on Friday but did not confirm direct talks with the US
key_facts.excerpt: Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi has landed in Pakistan, but Iranian media did not confirm talks with the US

key_facts.fact: Pentagon chief Pete Hegseth said the US blockade on Iranian ports will remain in place 'until necessary'
key_facts.excerpt: Iran and the US remain locked in a standoff over the Strait of Hormuz, with Pentagon chief Pete Hegseth saying blockade on Iranian ports will remain in place 'until necessary'

key_facts.fact: Israel and Lebanon agreed to extend the ceasefire by three weeks, Trump announced on Thursday
key_facts.excerpt: Israel and Lebanon agreed to extend the ceasefire by three weeks, US President Donald Trump said

key_facts.fact: The US froze $344 million in cryptocurrency assets linked to Iran as part of its pressure campaign on Tehran
key_facts.excerpt: The US has frozen $344 million (€239.5 million) in cryptocurrency assets over ties to Iran, the US Treasury Secretary said

key_facts.fact: This is the second attempt at peace talks; the first round in Islamabad was led by VP Vance nearly two weeks ago
key_facts.excerpt: Iran war: Second attempt at peace talks takes shape

stories.headline: Amazon-Backed Nuclear Startup X-Energy Raises $1.02B in Upsized IPO, Surges 31% on Debut

key_facts.fact: X-Energy priced IPO at $23/share, well above the marketed range of $16-$19, selling 44.3 million shares to raise $1.02 billion
key_facts.excerpt: X-energy priced its initial public offering at $23 per share, raising $1.02 billion in an upsized offering that came in above the marketed range of $16 to $19

key_facts.fact: Shares surged 30.9% in the Nasdaq debut, fetching a valuation of $11.9 billion
key_facts.excerpt: X-Energy shares surged 30.9% in their Nasdaq debut, fetching the company a valuation of $11.9 billion

key_facts.fact: X-Energy develops the Xe-100, a small modular reactor cooled by helium rather than water, and manufactures its own TRISO fuel
key_facts.excerpt: The Xe-100 is cooled by helium rather than the water used in conventional reactor designs

key_facts.fact: Amazon invested roughly $500 million in X-Energy in 2024 to accelerate SMR deployment; company has deals with Dow and Centrica
key_facts.excerpt: In 2024, X-energy received roughly $500 million from Amazon to accelerate deployment of its small modular reactor technology

key_facts.fact: Last year's financials showed ~$94M revenue against $390M in losses; a 2023 SPAC listing attempt was abandoned
key_facts.excerpt: Last year's financials showed roughly $94 million in revenue (excluding grants) against losses of about $390 million
